The write-ahead log is also known as a write-ahead logging (WAL). The file that contains the log is called the write-ahead log file. The log is written to before any data is written to the main database file. When you're using a write-ahead log, the database uses the log to verify the consistency of the database after a crash. If the database is damaged, the database can recover by replaying the log.
The write-ahead log is a mechanism that allows a database to recover after a crash by providing a record of all transactions that were applied to the database before the crash. Here's how it works: when a transaction is applied to the database, the database first writes a record of the transaction to the write-ahead log file. Only after the record has been written to the log is the transaction applied to the database. This way, even if the database crashes after writing the record to the log but before applying the actual transaction, the database can still recover by replaying the log.
After a crash, the database reads the write-ahead log from the file, and replays it, applying the transactions recorded in the log back to the database. The database verifies the consistency of the database by checking that the transactions apply correctly, and if any errors are detected
